subject.title: [Feature] Cron and subagent sessions lack user context for plugin OAuth tools

question: Should OpenClaw add a generic requester-identity contract for cron and subagent plugin OAuth tools, and which identity fields may unattended runs expose?
rationale: This changes plugin-visible OAuth authority for scheduled and spawned work, so automation cannot safely choose the permanent API shape or security posture.

options.title: Design Generic Requester Context
options.body: Add a typed runtime and Plugin SDK seam for explicit requester identity with consent, audit, privacy, and revocation rules before implementation.

options.title: Keep It Plugin-Owned For Now
options.body: Ask affected plugins to use local scheduled-identity configuration while core avoids a generic unattended user-context API.

options.title: Defer Pending Live Proof
options.body: Keep cron and spawned runs headless until maintainers have live evidence from more OAuth-dependent plugins.

recommendation.title: Design Generic Requester Context
recommendation.body: Add a typed runtime and Plugin SDK seam for explicit requester identity with consent, audit, privacy, and revocation rules before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest combined history across cron, sessions_spawn, subagent routing, and plugin requester context boundaries.
